cells.tense: Right now you are carrying what needs carrying and it is moving between people the way it should.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Decide on a direction you want more of a year from now, and give it thirty minutes this week — no surveying the rest.
cells.core:
You can carry what has to be carried and pass strength to the people near you in the same motion. It isn't hardness. You keep your shape under pressure without going stiff, so somebody's rough week can land on you and you stay level and hand something back that helps. Carrying and giving are one movement here, which is what makes it work.

What you feed with that strength is worth deciding rather than inheriting. The weight you take on for others is already settled; where the whole of you points next is not. Go by what you actually want, not what logic says it is sensible to want, and hold that heading through the first three days, when the pull is strongest and the newness is gone. It holds because you chose it.
cells.sheetLine: You carry the weight and pass the strength on.
cells.verb: Carrying more than your own weight so the people near you stay upright.
cells.place: Where you keep bearing what has to be borne and keep your form under it.

cells.tense: You are bracing under a load that has not actually landed on you yet.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: The next time the urge to pre-solve someone's problem shows up, do the small fair move your compass gives you, then leave the rest with them.
cells.core:
The strength going out from you gets to people before the moment they need it. You sense a problem forming a week off and start bearing it now, so the people beside you get steadiness before they have asked and sometimes before they know anything is wrong. The support is real. It has stopped waiting to be received, and you keep checking whether you are giving the right amount, which is the calculation all of this was meant to spare you.

When over-giving shows up in a small case, follow the compass once and stop. The person on the other end gets room to do their own part for once. Fairness that moves freely does not keep a running tally; it makes one honest move and then lets go. What contains without crushing is what you are reaching back toward.

cells.tense: Somewhere behind this moment you were holding your shape under pressure and today nothing is asking that of you.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Spend twenty minutes today on the hard part of something you keep circling — the actual difficulty, not the setting up.
cells.core:
Endurance is in you. You have carried weight before. Right now nothing is calling on it, and you stay a step back from the difficult part, watching it, keeping the forms up. The people who lean on you get a version of your strength. Not the full one. The firm ability to hold under load is still there, waiting, and it is not being asked for.

Go at the difficult thing on purpose, not by getting tougher first. Twenty minutes of real friction will tell you more than another week of getting ready. Some of it will hold. Some will turn out to have been the wrong shape and fall away, which is how the thing worth committing to gets found. The commitment is what gets tested. The method is what gets dropped.

cells.tense: The strength is moving between people and you are telling it as though someone else brought it.
cells.act: face one way for three days
cells.ask: Aim at something you have been quietly moving toward. Say nothing about it. Give it three days before you decide.
cells.core:
You are the one holding the line several people are currently standing behind. Ask and you would say it just kept things steady, that anyone would have done it. The people being held have not made that mistake — they know where the weight came from. What is missing is not the doing. It is your own account of it, and the direction running underneath, which has been steering without your attention on it.

There is a heading in you that took shape before you had words for it and has been setting the course with nobody watching. Put your attention there. Something you have been moving toward while telling yourself you were only handling what came up. Three days facing one way will show you what was already true. The turn comes before anyone else's.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it up and calling it someone else's.
cells.verb: Carrying more than your own weight so the people near you stay upright.
cells.place: Where you keep bearing what has to be borne and keep your form under it.
